sample_unit: questions (30 each for RAI, PRRT, TARE; 29 for PSMA-TRT), each asked to two chatbots

links.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading grade level of chatbot responses versus general public reading level
links.effect: Mean FKRGL for GPT-4 was 14.25-14.65 and for Bard 11.35-13.01 across RAI, PSMA-TRT, PRRT and TARE; all above the general public reading grade level.
links.quote: In terms of readability the FRKGL scores of the responses of GPT-4 and Google Bard about RAI, PSMA-TRT, PRRT and TARE treatments were above the general public reading grade level.

links.outcome: Readability of chatbot patient information responses relative to general public
links.effect: GPT-4 mean FKRGL 14.25-14.65 and Bard 11.35-13.01, above general public reading grade level, potentially preventing understanding.
links.quote: Although the information provided by AI chatbots may be acceptable in medical terms, it can not be easy to read for the general public, which may prevent it from being understandable.

unlisted_practices: Prompt engineering to make chatbot responses more comprehensible
Chatbot responses should name a nuclear medicine physician as consultant

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates the reliability (DISCERN) and readability (FKRGL/FRE) of baseline ChatGPT-4 and Google Bard responses to patient questions on radionuclide cancer treatments, but does not test or compare a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
